body:
16 Nov 2026, P2-25 slices 2+3, PR #110: SECOND-EYES REVIEW of head cc7a749, one BLOCKER fixed, concerns answered.
BLOCKER (the 'either ref' hold test could not fail on its loser half): the old test had BOTH refs on the worklist. New test test_refmerge_holds_a_pair_when_only_one_of_the_two_refs_is_on_the_worklist: an Arabic ref (on the worklist) and a Latin ref (never suspect) hold one library file; parametrized so the worklist ref is the survivor in one case and the loser in the other; each is held (recheck_pending), nothing moved (snapshot of every person table incl. a like), no backup taken, and a CONTROL: after DELETE FROM ref_recheck the same pair merges with the same survivor, so the worklist is the ONLY thing that held it. Mutation run: dropping the loser half of the guard turns only the [the loser] case red, dropping the survivor half turns only the [the survivor] case red; restored, green.
DOCS fixed (stale or misleading): design row 3 and audit B-37 no longer say the dry run is 'in the PR' as if the report were committed (counts are in the PR body and the board; the report with titles is a local file outside any git repo); the migration number text says 0018 (main has 0017); 'REFUSES' now reads 'REFUSES TO REWRITE ... it does not stop the server' with its cost. The slice 3 row states the COST UNTIL SLICE 4: nothing empties ref_recheck, so every pair with a worklist ref stays held and the N-11 duplicates stay duplicated on a Host with damaged library refs: slice 4 is a release gate for this PR (the order of release is the lead's call).
NOT CHANGED (concerns, not trivial): (1) the worklist and the hold judge only the ref's own text (non-ASCII or no letter); an all-ASCII ref with an empty-segment key ('Official Video', '(sic)') is not held, 1 of 3394 in the dry run; adding refs.key_is_degenerate of the stored key as a second reason is a small follow-up with its own rows. (2) refs.norm_key still runs on any Python: only the REWRITE is guarded; refuse-to-start is the lead's decision (PR decision 2). (3) a persistently failing repair takes a new VACUUM INTO copy at every start and nothing prunes backups/: reuse the copy of this revision, or log once (follow-up). (4) the plain YouTube scorer substring branches (wt in ct, wa in a) bypass the dense-script equality rule for 1 to 4 character Han or Kana names: weaker than docs/19 says.
VERIFICATION: whole server suite, ruff, ruff format, mypy encore_server, check_rows and check_order clean on Python 3.13.14 (Unicode 15.1.0); the new test does not depend on the Unicode version. The 3.12 venv of the earlier run no longer exists on this machine. The Lucene five-file hashes and the tag/commit label were checked by the earlier helper with network; not re-checked here.
